CrowdStrike just launched an AI Kill Switch.

Not a concept. Not a roadmap item. A production mechanism to halt AI agents operating in enterprise environments.

The same week, Adobe and Smartsheet shipped AI agents directly inside their tools. Your teams will interact with autonomous AI whether your governance is ready or not.

Here is why this matters: AI agent adoption is outpacing every control framework being built around it. Agent mentions in tech hiring now exceed LLM mentions — 14.8% versus 10.7%. The protocol agents use to communicate jumped from near-zero to 4.5% in job postings within a year.

Security vendors see the gap. CrowdStrike is positioning agent governance as a core market, not an add-on. When AI agents can access sensitive data, modify code, and trigger real-world actions, the ability to stop them instantly is table stakes.

The question for every business leader: do you know what your AI agents can access, what they can do autonomously, and who can shut them down?
